output_json.patch_notes:
Root cause: in FilenameUtils.getPrefixLength(), the UNC branch (isSeparator(ch0) && isSeparator(ch1)) returned the position after the first inner separator as the prefix length without validating the host-name segment between the leading "//" and that separator. For "//../foo", the segment ".." was accepted as a host name, so "//../" became the prefix and doNormalize() never resolved the ".." -> normalize returned "//../foo".

Fix (mirrors Apache Commons IO 2.7 / the CVE-2021-29425 patch):
- Added imports: java.util.Arrays, java.util.List, java.util.regex.Matcher, java.util.regex.Pattern.
- In getPrefixLength()'s UNC branch, compute the candidate prefix length and extract the host-name part (filename.substring(2, pos-1)); return that length only if isValidHostName(hostnamePart), otherwise NOT_FOUND.
- Added private helpers isValidHostName(), isIPv4Address(), isIPv6Address(), and isRFC3986HostName() (with supporting constants/patterns) copied from the upstream fix. Invalid host names such as ".." now cause getPrefixLength to return -1, which makes doNormalize() return null.

Verification:
- Provided PoV flipped from VULNERABLE (exit 0, normalize="//../foo") to NOT VULNERABLE (exit 1, normalize=null) after the patch, using the project's Docker wrapper.
- Added regression test testNormalizeUncPathTraversal in FilenameUtilsTestCase asserting normalize("//../foo"), "\\\\..\\foo", "//../", "//.." and an invalid-host UNC path all return null, while legitimate UNC paths ("//server/a", "//127.0.0.1/a") still normalize correctly.
- FilenameUtilsTestCase: 38/38 pass. Full suite: the only 4 failures (FileUtilsCleanDirectoryTestCase, FileFilterTestCase canRead/canWrite) are pre-existing and unrelated — they fail because tests run as root in the container (read-only/cannot-delete file semantics don't apply to root) and touch no code changed by this patch.
output_json.risk_notes: Behavioral change: FilenameUtils.normalize/getPrefixLength/getPrefix now reject UNC-style paths whose host-name segment is not a valid RFC 3986 reg-name or IP literal (e.g. "//..", "//foo bar/x"), returning null/-1 instead of a string. This is the intended, upstream-aligned security behavior and matches Commons IO >= 2.7; callers relying on the previous lax parsing of malformed UNC prefixes could see null where they previously got a (traversal-bearing) string. Valid UNC paths ("//server/share", IPv4/IPv6 hosts) are unaffected. No dependency changes; helper methods are private and copied verbatim from the official fix.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-022 / CVE-2021-29425 path traversal in Apache Commons IO's FilenameUtils. getPrefixLength() treated a leading double separator followed by any text as a UNC authority-style prefix, so inputs like "//../foo" had "//../" classified as an inviolable prefix and the ".." traversal segment survived normalize(), letting a path escape its intended directory. Applied the upstream Commons IO 2.7 fix: the UNC branch now validates the host-name portion (RFC 3986 reg-name or IPv4/IPv6 literal) and returns NOT_FOUND when it is invalid (e.g. ".."), so normalize("//../foo") now returns null and the traversal segment is neutralized.
